data.hypothesis: The prior valid 32x8 mapping averaged 3.004 μs and the 64x4 mapping averaged 3.120 μs, versus 3.494 μs for baseline; these results do not isolate a cause. This experiment keeps x-contiguous warp lanes and direct loads but uses 32x4 blocks (128 threads) and twice as many CTAs as 32x8. It tests whether smaller CTAs improve scheduling on the target enough to offset additional CTA overhead; no speedup is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: These measurements apply to the supplied 64³ stencil and measured target; they do not establish a universal best block shape.
memory_lessons.claim: Three distinct direct-global candidates were correct. The 32x8 mapping averaged 3.004 μs, 64x4 averaged 3.120 μs, and flattened averaged 3.278 μs; all were below the 3.494 μs baseline, but the results do not identify a causal bottleneck.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure a contrasting 32x4 mapping to test CTA size and grid count while keeping direct loads and contiguous-x warp lanes.

data.notes: This candidate is unmeasured. Controller should validate the independent oracle over its cases and compare full-run event latency; no performance result is claimed. Target facts used: NVIDIA GH200 and CUDA 12.6.3, as supplied in context. No commands were run.
transformations: Replace the shared-memory y-stencil kernel with a direct-global kernel assigning one output per thread, with no shared storage or block-wide barrier.
Use 32x4 blocks and a 2x16x64 grid, keeping warp lanes on contiguous x values while reducing threads per CTA from 256 to 128.
Explicitly load all eight y-neighbors and independently reproduce the baseline period-(my-1) halo mapping for each offset.
Retain the existing coefficients and run entry point; write the complete output with one kernel launch and no additional allocation.
